questions.question:
A reaction gives temperature rises of 12.4, 12.6, 8.1 and 12.5 °C.
Part (a): Identify the anomaly, calculate the mean of valid results, give a suitable uncertainty from the range.
Part (b): Suggest why the experimental rise may be below the true value.
questions.modelAnswer:
8.1 °C is anomalous.
Mean = (12.4 + 12.6 + 12.5)/3 = 12.5 °C.
Half range = (12.6 − 12.4)/2 = ±0.1 °C (accept range 0.2 °C if stated).
Lower value may result from heat loss to surroundings/apparatus, incomplete reaction, evaporation or delayed temperature reading.
markingPoints: 8.1 °C is anomalous.
Half range = (12.6 − 12.4)/2 = ±0.1 °C (accept range 0.2 °C if stated).

questions.question: Plan an investigation to find how changing the mass of calcium oxide affects the temperature change when it is added to water. Include the apparatus, method, control variables, repeats and how you would process the results.
questions.modelAnswer: Use an insulated polystyrene cup with a lid, thermometer/temperature probe, measuring cylinder, balance, water and calcium oxide. Measure a fixed volume of water and record its initial temperature. Add a measured mass of calcium oxide, fit the lid, stir and record the highest temperature. Calculate ΔT. Repeat with several different masses of calcium oxide, keeping the water volume, starting temperature, cup/lid, stirring and reading method the same. Repeat each mass, calculate a mean ΔT and identify anomalies. Wear eye protection because calcium oxide is irritant/corrosive; add it carefully to avoid splashes.
markingPoints: Use an insulated polystyrene cup with a lid, thermometer/temperature probe, measuring cylinder, balance, water and calcium oxide. Measure a fixed volume of water and record its initial temperature. Add a measured mass of calcium oxide, fit the lid, stir and record the highest temperature. Calculate ΔT. questions.question: Describe an experiment to measure the energy released by a neutralisation reaction?

Plot the highest temperatures against concentration.

questions.question:

Ea = 280 − 120 = 160 kJ/mol. ΔH = products − reactants = 70 − 120 = −50 kJ/mol.
Negative ΔH means exothermic.
Catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower peak/Ea.
It does not change reactant/product energy or ΔH.

Negative ΔH means exothermic.

questions.question: Explain energy changes in terms of bond breaking and bond making, including why a reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

Making bonds releases energy (exothermic).

Reverse gives endothermic.

questions.question:
Use bond energies H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 243 and H–Cl = 432 kJ/mol to calculate the energy change for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl.
State whether it is exothermic or endothermic and explain.
questions.modelAnswer:
Energy to break = 436 + 243 = 679 kJ/mol.
Energy released making = 2 × 432 = 864 kJ/mol. ΔH = bonds broken − bonds formed = 679 − 864 = −185 kJ/mol.
Exothermic because more energy is released making bonds than absorbed breaking them.
markingPoints: Energy to break = 436 + 243 = 679 kJ/mol.
Energy released making = 2 × 432 = 864 kJ/mol. ΔH = bonds broken − bonds formed = 679 − 864 = −185 kJ/mol.
Exothermic because more energy is released making bonds than absorbed breaking them.

Energy change would be written approximately −117 kJ/mol for the reaction.

questions.question: Calculate the overall energy change for the following reaction: H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl. Bond energies: H-H = 436 kj/ mol, Cl-Cl = 243 kJ/mol and H-Cl = 432 kJ/mol. State if the reaction is endothermic or exothermic?
questions.modelAnswer: Energy in = 436 (H-H) + 243 (Cl-Cl ) = 679kJ/mol. Energy out = (2 x 432)(2 x H -Cl) = 864kJ/mol; Energy change = energy in - energy out = 679 - 864 = -185kJ/mol; the energy change is negative so the reaction is exothermic.
markingPoints: Energy in = 436 (H-H) + 243 (Cl-Cl ) = 679kJ/mol. Energy out = (2 x 432)(2 x H -Cl) = 864kJ/mol; Energy change = energy in - energy out = 679 - 864 = -185kJ/mol; the energy change is negative so the reaction is exothermic.

questions.question: Calculate the overall energy change for the following reaction: 2HBr → H2 + Br2. Bond energies: H-H = 436 kJ/mol, Br-Br = 193 kJ/mol and H-Br = 366 kJ/mol. State if the reaction is endothermic or exothermic?
questions.modelAnswer: Energy in = (2 x 366)(2 x H-Br) = 732 kJ/mol; Energy out = 436 (H-H) + 193 (Br-Br) = 629kJ/mol; Energy change = energy in - energy out = 732 - 629 = + 103kJ/mol; the energy change is positive so the reaction is endothermic.
